title: Case, new grad product manager, average answers

questions.text: FreshCart is a grocery delivery app in one city. Fewer customers are ordering a second time. How would you think about that?
Estimate how many orders FreshCart handles in one day in a city of one million people.
You have three ideas: faster delivery slots, a loyalty program, and better substitutions when items are out. Which would you do first?
Who is the main user of a school lunch ordering app?
How would you decide whether to launch FreshCart in a second city?
Estimate how many delivery drivers FreshCart needs at the evening peak.

probe_areas: No work experience in product yet

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Tomas, I'm Dana, a product manager here. This is a thirty minute product case conversation, and we will talk out loud.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Dana, nice to meet you. Thanks for the time.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How is your week going?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Pretty good. I am finishing my last exams, so it is busy.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Okay. I will give you two or three product questions. There is no single right answer, so think out loud and ask me anything.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: FreshCart is a grocery delivery app in one city. Fewer customers are ordering a second time. How would you think about that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think the main problem is probably delivery time or prices. So I would make delivery faster and add discounts for second orders. Maybe also send push notifications to remind people. I would also improve the app design so it feels nicer to use.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Before ideas, what would you want to know about the people who do not come back?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Okay. I would ask who they are, new customers or older ones, and when they stop. If most people leave after a late delivery, then speed matters. If they leave after missing items, then it is about stock. I would look at the data for the last three months first.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Next, an estimate. How many orders does FreshCart handle in one day in a city of one million people?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think it is maybe fifty thousand orders a day. A big city has many people and they order groceries often. So it should be quite a lot, but I am not sure about the exact number.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you get to that number?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Let me try again. One million people, about three per household, so around 330 thousand households. If one in ten uses the app, that is 33 thousand households. Maybe each orders once a week, so around 5 thousand orders a day.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: You have three ideas: faster delivery slots, a loyalty program, and better substitutions when items are out. Which would you do first?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think the loyalty program is good because people like rewards. Customers come back when they get points. But faster slots are also important. I would probably start with loyalty and then do the others later.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks, that is the end of the cases. What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: How do product managers on your team use data in a normal week?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Most of us look at a dashboard every Monday, then pick one question to study more deeply that week.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That's all the time we have. Thanks Tomas, the recruiter will follow up within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Dana. I enjoyed it.

notes: Average for new grad: some structure after a probe, rough numbers, weak recommendation.
